title: Behavioral Mutation Testing: Do Small Prompt Mutations Reveal the Same Fragile Mode in Every Model?

original_idea.body:
# Behavioral Mutation Testing

Generate systematic small prompt mutations around safety-relevant decision points and build a cross-model kill matrix; a column where one mutation flips every model identically reveals a universally shared fragile boundary. Inference (arXiv:2010.09144).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 3: plausible chain (shared fragile boundary = correlated exploit surface) but the catastrophic link is somewhat generic.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 5: generate small mutations, build a cross-model kill matrix; standard tooling.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 4: focused kill-matrix deliverable; designing systematic mutations adds a dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: open models + simple mutations, no internal access, weak lab incentive.

novelty.reasoning: Behavioral mutation testing for shared cross-model fragility appears largely novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Mutation testing applied to cross-model shared fragility is plausibly novel.
